proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_reroll
proposed_widenings.justification: Indomitable's core mechanic is rerolling a failed saving throw. This is distinct from advantage (roll two dice simultaneously, take higher) and from modify_roll_numeric (additive delta to a single roll). The reroll replaces the failed result after it is known. modify_roll_reroll is present in the v4 taxonomy (TAXONOMY_atoms_graph.md §9 Effect Atoms) but absent from types.ts EffectAtom.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll.

proposed_widenings.name: ReactionTrigger.fail_saving_throw
proposed_widenings.justification: Indomitable triggers on ANY failed saving throw, not just saves against spells. The existing spell_save_outcome trigger is described as a 'Post-save spell reflection / conversion window' narrowed to saves against spells. A new trigger variant is needed: { kind: 'fail_saving_throw' } (or { kind: 'saving_throw_outcome'; outcome: 'failure' }) with no spell-source constraint. This enables the reaction/activation cost to correctly gate the reroll window.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it...

proposed_widenings.name: DiceDelta.class_level
proposed_widenings.justification: The reroll bonus is 'equal to your Fighter level' — a class-level-scaled numeric bonus. The current DiceDelta variants are: fixed_dice, proficiency_bonus, ability_modifier, magic_item_rarity_bonus. None models a raw class level. A new variant { kind: 'class_level'; className: ClassName; sign: '+' | '-' } is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level

notes: The use-count scaling (1@L9, 2@L13, 3@L17) maps cleanly to ThresholdTiers<number> with axis='class'. The long-rest reset maps cleanly to RestResetCadence { kind: 'long_rest' }. The activation cost family (reaction triggered by failing a save) maps to ClassFeatureActivationCost.reaction. All three blockers are surface gaps against existing v4 atoms or clearly-needed new variants of existing surface types; none require a new top-level mechanics family. No dhall/json/trace produced.
